entries.name: Abomination
entries: {@i Unholy Combination of Stitched Dead Flesh}

Abominations are flesh constructs made from the reanimated body parts of mutilated corpses. Held together by loose stitching and pieces of metal and bone, they reek of death and disease, dangling entrails and dripping fluids from open wounds as they bound relentlessly forward, cleavers in hand. Though their lolling heads and gaping mouths appear almost joyful, they are driven by little more than their desire to carve through and consume flesh, whether it belongs to the living or the dead.

entries.name: Aku'mai
entries: This three-headed ancient evil carries within it a seed of the {@book Old Gods'|WoW|6|Old Gods} power. {@creature Lady Sarevess|WoW} believes it is the spawn of N'Zoth and a key to opening his nightmare realm of Ny'alotha. Aku'mai is feared by all for its relentless savagery and insatiable hunger—but the wise fear it because all who look on it hear the whispers of the Old Gods.

entries.name: Alleria Windrunner
entries: {@i Void-Infused Elf Who Guides Her Kin}

The eldest Windrunner sister, Alleria is a light in the darkness for her people—or perhaps she is darkness within the light. The Alliance knows her best as a hero of the Second War, venerated alongside her peers with a towering statue in Stormwind City's Valley of Heroes. Like them, she was thought to have died in Outland.

Alleria and her husband, the human paladin Turalyon, became warriors of the Light and journeyed deep into the Twisting Nether to fight the {@book Burning Legion|WoW|6|Burning Legion} on far-flung worlds. In this time, Alleria dabbled in forbidden magic, and gained the power of the Void. She returned to Azeroth after forty years away, though the time dilation of the Twisting Nether made it like a thousand years of war to her. Though she was feared by the Army of Light, she was admitted into the Alliance and trained a cohort of elves to welcome shadow into their own bodies and become void elves like her.

Though still at odds with her husband, Alleria has tried to rebuild her bond with her estranged son, Arator, and her former homeland of Quel'Thalas. More than anything, she craves connection, as her desire for enough power to protect those she loves inevitably drives them away. She swears she can remain in control of her Void powers, but those close to her fear that her control will fail.

entries.name: Alzzin the Wildshaper

entries: O Felvine, as the Fruit of Fertility you gave this verdant land life. Now, drain it dry, and gift its power unto me!

Alzzin was once a night elf druid but now leads the Wildspawn cult. Before he was corrupted into a satyr millennia ago, he obsessed over the work of a Highborn named Millicent Serene, who created the Fruit of Fertility, a conduit to the Emerald Dream that turned Feralas into the lush jungle that it is today. Millicent died in the War of the Ancients, and Alzzin's obsession shifted to her crowning achievement—namely, corrupting it into the Felvine, which drains the life from Feralas and empowers him.

entries.name: Ancient of War
entries: {@i Protector of Nature in Tree Form}

Ancients of War are protectors of nature and guardians of life that take the form of giant sentient trees. Though they can appear to be ordinary trees when motionless, they hold deep wisdom, cultivated over lives that last for thousands of years and preserved through memories that are as long as their roots are deep. Ancients can sense disturbances in the world through their roots and provide power and protection to those who would keep the world and its natural places safe.

Ancients of War bear bark like iron scarred with the marks of ten thousand years of battles. They patrol the deep forests of Kalimdor with their night elf allies and lead the charge against those who would defile their domain.

entries.name: Anduin Wrynn
entries: {@i King of Stormwind and Commander of the Alliance}

Anduin Wrynn is the king of Stormwind. Beloved by his people, the Young Lion has been the target of assassination, manipulation, and kidnapping attempts all his life, yet it never stopped his kind heart from seeking peace between the Alliance and its foes.

His bold and martial father, King Varian Wrynn, died horribly at the hands of the {@book Burning Legion|WoW|6|Burning Legion}, testing tender Anduin's mettle when he took the throne in the midst of a demonic invasion. Now that the existential threat of the Legion has been defeated, the old tensions between the Alliance and the Horde have reignited. Anduin must ask himself: Can he still lead his people peacefully when friends and foes alike clamor for war? Can he be true to his own heart, when his allies long for him to be his father?
This stat block and character description represents Anduin as the king of Stormwind, as he appears in {@i Battle for Azeroth} and beyond.

entries.name: Anub'arak

entries: I was king of this empire once, long ago. In life I stood as champion. In death I returned as conqueror. Now I protect the kingdom once more. Ironic, yes?

The Traitor King of the nerubians, Anub'arak, fought tirelessly against the Scourge until his death. Now, the prideful king is a lapdog of the {@creature Lich King Arthas|WoW|Lich King}, guarding Azjol-Nerub from Alliance and Horde forces that would use it as a passage into Icecrown, as he once did. Anub'arak throws himself recklessly into every fight, perhaps hoping to die and finally be free of the Lich King's domination.

entries.name: Arcanist Doan

entries: You will not defile this archive's mysteries!
Doan was a renowned scholar of purifying magic, particularly cleansing flame. These days, he stews in the monastery's library, mistrusted by the Crusade's leaders and longing to prove himself.

entries.name: Baron Ashbury

entries: Tally ho! The hunt begins!

A noble of Gilneas and a patriot who betrayed his king, Baron Ashbury was raised as an undead Forsaken when {@creature Sylvanas Windrunner|WoW|Sylvanas Windrunner's} army attacked his homeland. Now an enemy of both the worgen of Gilneas and the Forsaken, he serves the only master left to him: {@creature Lord Godfrey|WoW}.

entries.name: Baron Silverlaine

entries: Leave this accursed place at once!

Baron Silverlaine was master of Shadowfang Keep before it fell to Arugal's feral worgen. His cursed spirit calls on the beasts that slaughtered him to punish trespassers. He is bound to the stones of the keep and has no loyalty to {@creature Lord Godfrey|WoW|Godfrey} or any of the keep's masters.

entries.name: Black Dragonflight
entries: {@i Warders of the Earth Corrupted to Evil}

The black dragonflight has power over earth and flame and was charged in ancient times with protecting the deep places of the earth. This flight was corrupted by the whispers of the Old Gods imprisoned beneath the earth and fell to evil. The dragons now lair in sweltering, desolate places such as Blackrock Mountain and Dustwallow Marsh, ruled by the children of Deathwing that revel in mortal suffering. The corrupted black dragons are the enemies of every other dragonflight, especially the noble red dragonflight.
Who would have thought someone named Deathwing would bring about so much destruction?

Fully matured black dragonflight dragons terrorize the lands of Azeroth from the skies and manipulate society by shape-shifting into humanoid disguises. A black dragon wearing a mortal visage usually has jet-black hair and red eyes.

Black dragonflight drakes use their magic to heat objects made of earth or stone. They can momentarily melt stone into magma and reshape it before it cools. These drakes delight in stalking and disorienting prey.

Black dragonflight whelps are murderous little creatures that dwell near volcanoes, hot springs, and geysers. They smother prey in their magma breath and pick the meat from the globs of scalding lava.

entries.name: Bloodmage Thalnos

entries: We hunger for vengeance.

Thalnos earned repute in the Scarlet Crusade for the brutal, lustrating tortures he inflicted on new recruits. The sadistic mage contracted the plague of undeath but kept his mind. Now he is tormented by his fellow crusaders, who wish to wipe him out even though he craves their blessings.

entries.name: Blue Dragonflight
entries: {@i Protectors of Ancient Magic}

The blue dragonflight was devastated by the evil Deathwing and his black dragonflight. Now led by Kalecgos, the Steward of Magic, the blue dragonflight is enjoying a resurgence, and these dragons' magical powers are awesome to behold. Their freezing breath and gargantuan claws have been the death of many foolish intruders in Azeroth's mountains and arctic regions.

Blue dragonflight dragons view themselves as stewards of the arcane, and they disdain mortals who misuse their gifts. Noble blue dragons take the role of sagely mentors to mortal mages—for example, Kalecgos long worked with the Kirin Tor in a mortal visage. Cruel and jealous blue dragons such as Cyanigosa try to dominate and punish mortals for their misuse of magic.
Members of the blue dragonflight are devoted students of the arcane arts. Blue dragonflight drakes learn to create and dispel magical effects, protecting their secrets from prying mages.
Blue dragonflight whelps display uncanny intelligence for their age. Rather than attacking an ice fisher, a blue whelp might ask to pool their knowledge, striking a deal to share the fish they catch.

entries.name: Bronze Dragonflight
entries: {@i Guardians of Time}

Ruled by Nozdormu the Timeless One, the bronze dragonflight guards the timeways of Azeroth. These stoic guardians maintain the delicate balance of past, present, and future, and they can facilitate time travel by opening time portals. The people of Azeroth often see bronze dragons as cold and unfeeling, since the dragons prefer not to interfere in mortal affairs.

Bronze dragons' enemies, the infinite dragonflight, are led by Murozond, a version of Nozdormu from an alternate timeline that seeks to "perfect" the timeline by altering key moments in history. Infinite dragonflight dragons use the same statistics as bronze dragonflight dragons.

Mature bronze dragons task themselves with maintaining the one true timeline of Azeroth. They keep close to humanoid civilizations, watching for travelers from other timelines or those who seek to alter the timeways.

Many a villain has tried to bend a bronze dragonflight drake to their will, hoping to take advantage of the creature's prophetic magic while the drake is still young. Such opportunists quickly learn the error of their ways when the bronze drake shreds and sears their skin with its red-hot sand breath.

Bronze dragonflight whelps are patient. They stand still for hours on end in the middle of the desert, waiting for prey to pass before striking out with maw or claw. Many travelers mistake these whelps for statues.

entries.name: Captain Greenskin

entries: Avast, ye swabs! Repel the invaders!
The Juggernaut's captain is a disgraced buccaneer called Greenskin. He doesn't trust Sneed and Gilnid but doesn't mind captaining the ship they're building.
Captain Greenskin's first mate is Mister Smite, a tauren {@creature Warrior Veteran|XMM}. His cook is Cookie, a {@creature Murloc Oracle|WoW}.

entries.name: Cho'Rush the Observer

entries: What, we cheat? (Yeah, huh huh, we cheat.) Hush!

The two-headed ogre mage Cho'Rush doesn't usually take sides, but when Ulrok was rising to power, it was clear nobody could challenge him. Cho'Rush ingratiated himself to Ulrok by healing him in the bloodbath that made him king. As a reward, the new King Gordok awarded Cho'Rush the position of chief adviser.
If revealed as a cheat (see "{@book Ogre Tribute|WoW|6|Ogre Tribute}" above), Cho'Rush abandons all pretense and fights openly.

entries.name: Commander Springvale

entries: Intruders in the keep! To arms!

Commander Springvale unquestioningly served Baron Silverlaine in the old days. Springvale died on the walls defending his liege lord and patrols them still, unaware that his castle is overrun and his allies are now rotten, shambling corpses.
I tend to believe that restless spirits and all other beings deserve a nice, long rest.

entries.name: Doomguard
entries: {@i Brutal Destroyer from the Burning Legion}

Powerful and deliberate, doomguard are winged demons of the {@book Burning Legion|WoW|6|Burning Legion} known across the cosmos for their brutality. Also called ered'ruin, doomguard are devoted to their {@creature Pit Lord|WoW} masters and revel in the destruction of worlds.
Doomguard sport furry, cloven-hoofed legs and formidable horns. Soaring through the skies, they swoop down to ram into foes or shake the earth with thunderous stomps.

entries.name: Edwin VanCleef

entries: Lapdogs, all of you!

Edwin VanCleef's sinister charisma was honed by Matthias Shaw, the head of Stormwind Intelligence (SI:7). VanCleef refused this calling, though, for the humble trade of a guild organizer, to better the lives of the common folk. If his cunning hadn't been polluted by vengeance, he could have truly changed the world for the better.

entries.name: Fel Imp
entries: {@i Gleeful Demon of Fel Flames}

Fel imps are mischievous demons that cackle with glee while immolating their foes in fel flames. They are the weakest forces of the {@book Burning Legion|WoW|6|Burning Legion}, but their small size leads enemies to underestimate the power of their firebolts.
Fel imps are the easiest demons for Warlocks to bind and control, making them common familiars for those who make pacts with the Burning Legion.
Through all time and space, there's more power hidden in the smallest things than you will ever know.

entries.name: Felguard
entries: {@i Foot Soldier of the Burning Legion}

Conscripted from the demonic mo'arg species, felguard serve as the {@book Burning Legion's|WoW|6|Burning Legion} rank-and-file soldiers. They are fearless and unwaveringly loyal to Sargeras's godlike will.

entries.name: Felhound
entries: {@i Demonic Hound with a Nose for Magic}
Felhounds are demonic canines used by pit lords to sniff out sources of magic. Unlike most demons, which are born of corrupted mortals, felhounds are shaped from raw fel energy.
Felhounds feed on magic, and they are fond of draining the energies of hapless wizards with the grasping tentacles on their back, then ripping the wizards' bodies to shreds.
No! Bad doggie... hound... fel... thing! Get your tentacles off my codex!
Felsworn satyrs wield the fiery power of the Burning Legion as its devoted agents. They are fierce enemies of night elves, using their magic to devastate night elf communities.

entries.name: Foreman Rhahk'Zor

entries: VanCleef pay big for your heads!
Foreman Rhahk'Zor is a brutish ogre grappler who betrayed his kin in the Deadmines when VanCleef arrived. He cares only about wealth and power and will sacrifice anyone to ensure his own survival.
Furbolg totemics are shaman who use totems for healing and offense.
Ursas are warrior leaders in furbolg tribes, larger than their kin and empowered by elemental magic.

entries.name: Furbolgs
entries: {@i Bearlike People of Secluded Woodlands}

Bearlike furbolgs live in family groups across northern Kalimdor, Northrend, and several island regions. They fought alongside night elves and tauren against the {@book Burning Legion|WoW|6|Burning Legion} in the War of the Ancients, though they prefer to live separate from other peoples. Furbolg traditions involve shamanic control of the elements. Some furbolgs have been corrupted and fallen under the sway of the Burning Legion, the Old Gods, or the Primalists. (Use the {@creature Cultist|XMM} stat blocks from the {@book Monster Manual|XMM} for these furbolgs.)

entries.name: Gelihast

entries: Mrr? Mrr! Mrrrglglglgl!!

The {@book Old God|WoW|6|Old Gods} called, and Gelihast answered, forcing his way into Blackfathom Deeps and slaughtering nearly a dozen surprised Twilight's Hammer cultists. Impressed by his brutality, the cult allowed him to stay, and he built his own shrine to offer sacrifices to the ominous presence in the temple ruins.
Gelihast's Blindlight murlocs think they control this cave, unaware that the Twilight's Hammer tolerates them only so long as they deter invaders.

entries.name: Ghamoo-Ra

entries: Grrrooooooooakk!

When the Twilight's Hammer cult took over Blackfathom, its followers tormented a snapjaw for years until it became vicious. Naming the beast Ghamoo-Ra, the cultists trained it to defend their shrine. If attacked from beyond its island, it pursues its attackers to the edge of the Pool of Ask'ar area, then retreats into the water and takes a Short Rest.

entries.name: Gilnid

entries: Anyone want a break? Too bad! Back to work, oafs!

Gilnid was renowned in Booty Bay for his unusually large size and for making mechanical bodyguards. He was exiled after his machines went haywire and slaughtered their charges. The Defias found him and paid him well to arm the Juggernaut; Gilnid is using the money to fund his pet project, a harvest golem called the Foe Reaper 4000. Early prototypes of the Foe Reaper guard the foundry. Gilnid is a coward who taunts his foes from behind his reapers.

entries.name: Green Dragonflight
entries: {@i Graceful Protectors of Life and Nature}

Green dragons serve nature and uphold the balance between mortal creatures and the ever-evolving world. The green dragonflight, originally ruled by the dreaming Aspect Ysera, holds a special love for the night elves and their druids. Though most green dragons live in the mystical dimension known as the Emerald Dream, some roam ancient forests where the veil between Azeroth and the Dream is thin.

This connection makes green dragons susceptible to the corrupting evil of the Emerald Nightmare. A Nightmare-corrupted green dragon has blackened scales pushed apart by pulsing red veins. Its stat block has the following changes:

items: It has Resistance to Necrotic damage instead of Acid damage.
Its Emerald Gas Breath action deals Necrotic damage instead of Acid damage (but still deals Poison damage).

entries: Spending time with the green dragonflight always makes me sleepy.

The mightiest of the green dragonflight battle the minions of the Old Gods and shape-shift into mortal visage forms to ally with humanoids. This battle against the Old Gods puts green dragons at risk for corruption by the Emerald Nightmare, which was created by one of the Old Gods' greatest champions.

Emerging from the Emerald Dream, green dragonflight drakes are wise enough to take action in Azeroth. They often ally with older dragons, night elf druids, and ancients of lore to eliminate evil cults and invading demons with nature magic.

Members of the green dragonflight raise their whelps in the Emerald Dream whenever possible. There, a whelp learns to appreciate and spread the beauty of nature in all its forms by observing cycles of birth and death.

entries.name: Hadronox

entries: SKREEEEEE!

During the fall of Azjol-Nerub, nerubian viziers released a single spider that would one day grow to challenge the unyielding forces of the {@creature Lich King Arthas|WoW|Lich King}. Hadronox was instilled with a desire to avenge the fallen and reclaim its home from any that dare threaten it.

{@creature Anub'arak|WoW|Anub'arak's} minions fight relentlessly (but fruitlessly) to drive Hadronox from their realm. When the characters breach the Gilded Gate, these minions turn to fight the characters. Hadronox temporarily acts as the characters' ally against Anub'arak's minions—but only for a moment. Hadronox craves the taste of fresh flesh and eagerly fights the characters as soon as the nerubians are destroyed.

entries.name: High Inquisitor Sally Whitemane

entries: The Light has spoken, for it has found you wanting.

Sally Whitemane was young when the plague of undeath swept through Lordaeron, and she was forced to raise a blade against her family—mother, father, brothers, sisters—as they turned into the Lich King's mindless pawns. She doesn't hold the ideals of the Crusade, but she swore to support her childhood friend Renault Mograine's quest to destroy undead at any cost.

entries.name: Houndmaster Loksey

entries: Release the hounds!

Loksey has loved dogs since he was a child, but the fanatical crusade convinced him it was right to send them into war to die. He thinks only purging the unclean can wash the canine blood from his hands.

entries.name: Illidan Stormrage
entries: {@i First of the Demon Hunters}

Illidan Stormrage is the first demon hunter and bears a demon hunter's sinister wings, curling horns, and fel-green eyes. Originally a powerful night elf mage, he was dubbed "The Betrayer" for aiding the {@book Burning Legion|WoW|6|Burning Legion} during the War of the Ancients and was imprisoned for ten thousand years by his twin brother, Archdruid Malfurion Stormrage.

Unknown to his brother or his beloved, Tyrande Whisperwind, Illidan sought the Legion's power to wield it against them and save his people. Now free from his imprisonment, he has fled into the Twisting Nether to evade his pursuers. There, he trains other elves as demon hunters and leads raids against the Burning Legion across the cosmos, but he trusts no living soul, mortal or demonic.

entries.name: Illyanna Ravenoak

entries: Flee... please! My will is not my own! It is the prince!

Illyanna Ravenoak and her animal companion Ferra were Prince Tortheldrin's most valued hunters until Illyanna refused the order to massacre her kin. As punishment, the prince executed Illyanna and used fel magic to bind her spirit to her corpse, condemning her to patrol his realm as an undead guard.
Illyanna's bear Ferra uses the {@creature Primeval Owlbear|XMM} stat block but has the Undead creature type.

entries.name: Immol'thar

entries: Guorrrr... GUORRRR!
Immol'thar is a void terror conjured from the Twisting Nether. The creature's fel blood generates vast amounts of magic, which the Shen'dralar siphon hourly.

entries.name: Infernal
entries: {@i Mindless Construct of Flame and Fury}

Infernals are crafted by mighty demons and summoned by warlocks' magic. Falling to the earth as yellow-green, molten meteorites, infernals exist only to destroy every living thing in their path. Infernals have destroyed entire cities before their energies dissipated back into the Twisting Nether.
Burning rocks that fall from space: super cool!
Fel burning rocks that crash to the ground: super not cool!

entries.name: Jaina Proudmoore
entries: {@i The Most Powerful Archmage Alive}

Jaina Proudmoore's people called her the Daughter of the Sea. She left behind her life in the nautical kingdom of Kul Tiras to study under the greatest archmages of the age in Dalaran. After the Third War, she became a legendary archmage of the {@book Kirin Tor|WoW|4|Kirin Tor} but has been forced to guard her heart, lest she suffer the pain of betrayal once more.

Jaina's hopes for peace died during the Cataclysm, when the bloodthirsty new Warchief of the Horde, Garrosh Hellscream, bombed her city of Theramore into oblivion. The Horde was no longer to be trusted, despite her friendship with {@creature Thrall|WoW}. From this nadir, she must discover who she truly is: the icy-hearted archmage she has been forced to become or the hopeful person she once was.

entries.name: King Gordok

entries: You challenge me, scrubs? I stay da king FOREVER!

To rule the Gordok ogres, one must simply proclaim oneself king, then destroy all who disagree. A devious Gordrunni warlord called Ulrok convinced a dozen of his people's strongest warriors to challenge the king at the same time. The wild melee left most of the contestants dead or wounded, and Ulrok's blade easily cut down the survivors and the battle-weary king. To this day, Gordrunni ogres speak in hushed tones about the "Day of Da Blood."

Gordok is so feared that he rarely faces any challenges, but he keeps his skills sharp as an undefeated champion of the Maul. He never picks a fight he doesn't think he can win—and cheats by having his vizier Cho'Rush discreetly heal him from afar.
All these King Gordoks... or is it Kings Gordok? Anyway, I think all big ogres would benefit from spending some time small.

entries.name: Krik'thir the Gatewatcher

entries: This kingdom belongs to the Scourge. Only the dead may enter!

When the Scourge first came to Northrend, Krik'thir was in charge of defending the gates of Azjol-Nerub. He fell in battle against the Scourge forces, and he was raised to undeath. He still holds the key that grants access to the lower reaches of the ancient city, but now he guards it for the Scourge.

entries.name: Lady Sarevess

entries: Armed and unbound? My servants have failed, then. No matter, a lively death will please my masters greatly!

Lady Sarevess is a self-proclaimed student of Queen Azshara, who created the naga long ago through a pact with the {@book Old God|WoW|6|Old Gods} N'Zoth. Lady Sarevess is obsessed with re-creating Queen Azshara's communion with the Old Gods. Sarevess disdains the Twilight's Hammer but lends them her strength and the might of her naga warriors so she can plunder the cultists' arcane lore.

entries.name: Lich King Arthas
entries: {@i Heir to the Frozen Throne}

The day Arthas was born, the forests of Lordaeron whispered his name. Under strict tutelage, the beloved prince bloomed into a mighty paladin, but pride festered in his noble heart. He thought himself capable of singlehandedly protecting Lordaeron from threat. Yet when he was outmatched, he discarded his allies and sought power at any cost.

That power came to him in {@item Frostmourne|WoW}, the cursed blade of Ner'zhul the Lich King. He took the blade to end the Cult of the Damned that spread an plague of undeath across his land, but he became the Lich King's pawn. In the end, he engulfed his homeland in the plague he sought to save it from, and in time he even donned the {@item Helm of Domination|WoW}, which contained the Lich King's spirit.

With Arthas's body and soul merged with the will of the Lich King, it's unclear whether a trace of his former self remains. He seems utterly remorseless, but it's possible some trace of the paladin he used to be is still capable of mercy.

entries.name: Lord Godfrey

entries: Reduced to ashes... Soon nothing will be left of Gilneas or the worgen taint.

Lord Vincent Godfrey of {@book Gilneas|WoW|4|Gilneas Renown Perks} saw the worgen curse ravage his kingdom. All his life, he had positioned himself to be the true power behind the Gilnean throne, but he broke when he learned that King Genn Greymane had become a worgen. Godfrey threw his life's work away to spite Greymane. Godfrey and his toady, {@creature Baron Ashbury|WoW}, tried to trade Greymane to the Forsaken in exchange for peace. His attempt failed, and he took his own life on the rocks of the Gilnean coast rather than live in a kingdom of wolves.

The Val'kyr found his shattered corpse and raised him as a Forsaken, though he didn't swear allegiance to {@creature Sylvanas Windrunner|WoW|Sylvanas} and managed to temporarily incapacitate her when he ransacked Pyrewood Village and conquered the keep overlooking it. Now, hated by both the Alliance and the Horde, he lurks within Shadowfang Keep, hatching a scheme that will allow him to emerge the one true victor in the war for Gilneas.

entries.name: Lord Walden

entries: Missing pages, broken equipment, tainted samples! How does someone work in these conditions?

The arrogant Lord Walden, {@creature Lord Godfrey|WoW|Godfrey's} right-hand man, vowed to pay any price, including death, to serve his compatriot and keep his power. He has adopted the vile alchemy of the Forsaken with aplomb.

entries.name: Moonkin
entries: {@i Moon-Blessed Guardian of Sacred Nature}

Moonkin, which resemble an antlered cross between a bear and a large owl, are believed by many to have been made by the moon goddess Elune to guard her sanctuaries. Moonkin often work alongside night elves and the green dragonflight to purify moonwells, defend against corrupted furbolgs, and halt deforestation. Moonkin are generally peaceful, but they lash out when nature is unbalanced by evil magic.

Moonkin carry the blessing of Elune, giving them a deep connection to the moon. Through Elune's blessing, they share the grace and beauty of their druidic magic with those they encounter and can call on Elune's power to strike those who act contrary to her purpose.

entries.name: Wildkin
entries: Wildkin are a lesser form of moonkin, less infused with Elune's magic and more like wild beasts than druidic protectors. Use the {@creature Primeval Owlbear|XMM} stat block in the {@book Monster Manual|XMM} for ordinary wildkin.

Murloc foragers live near the edges of bodies of water, spending most of their time searching for food in the mud and shallow waters. Of all murlocs, foragers are the most likely to be found outside of a group, and they often serve as an early warning system to their community, drawing would-be attackers to the water's edge for their fellow murlocs to ambush.
Oracles lead groups of other murlocs, using magic to defend and heal their allies. Murloc oracles are more willing than other murlocs to attempt communication with those who don't speak Nerglish.

entries.name: Murlocs
entries: {@i Amphibious People of Coastal Waters}

Since murlocs emerged from the oceans of Azeroth, these amphibious, piscine raiders have been steadily moving inland, forming communities along the banks of freshwater lakes and rivers. Murloc communities are close knit and insular, defending against conquest with simple weapons and elemental magic.
Murlocs were once forced to serve the naga as disposable workers and warriors, and their emergence onto land might be driven by a desire to avoid that fate.

Though some dismiss murlocs as pawns in larger conflicts, and very few understand the murlocs' primary language, Nerglish, murlocs are strategic fighters who use their ability to breathe, maneuver, and fight in both air and water to their advantage. Murlocs are also willing to sacrifice for one another, using sheer numbers to make up for their individual weakness.

In addition to the stat blocks presented here, any of the Humanoid stat blocks in the {@book Monster Manual|XMM} can be murlocs. For murlocs, add a Swim Speed equal to the creature's Speed plus 10 feet and the Amphibious trait from the stat blocks here. See the "{@book Furbolgs, Murlocs, and Quilboar|WoW|7|Furbolgs, Murlocs, and Quilboar}" sidebar for suggestions on other Humanoid stat blocks to use for murloc NPCs.
Nozdormu says I have the memory of a murloc, which is why I always write things down.

entries.name: N'raqi
entries: {@i Faceless Emissaries of the Old Gods}

After the Old Gods embedded themselves deep within Azeroth, their inky essence slowly seeped from their bodies, eventually coalescing into the n'raqi. Also called the Faceless, n'raqi dwell in shadows and cast eldritch spells in the dread tongue of Shath'Yar from tentacle-draped mouths. They are unflinchingly loyal heralds of the cosmic evils to whom they owe their existence. Whether they are marshalling the Old Gods' followers into armies, aiding cults, or doing the Old Gods' personal bidding, n'raqi are intelligent, dangerous, and powerful.

Lesser n'raqi called k'thir lurk in the shadows, often disguised as humans, and manipulate mortals' minds. These n'raqi use the {@creature Mind Flayer|XMM} stat block from the {@book Monster Manual|XMM}, and they speak Shath'Yar.
I've seen both a past and a possible future with the Old Gods in charge and faceless ones everywhere. That was enough for me.

Faceless generals, also called C'Thraxxi, lead the Old Gods' armies and defend their strongholds. Each C'Thrax has a deep well of magical ability, which it deploys to rip through the minds of those who get in its way, often leaving nothing more than drained husks in its wake. Even death is not a final end for these harbingers of doom; cultists have often tried, sometimes successfully, to awaken long-dead C'Thraxxi through sinister rituals and offerings of blood.

A faceless general's hulking form is covered in chitinous plates. Both its arms end in heavy pincers, and crablike legs sprout from its back, almost resembling wings. Each individual C'Thrax has its own unique characteristics, often reflective of the particular Old God it serves. For example, the Fury of N'Zoth has many eyes on its head and upper body, much like the Old God N'Zoth, while Warbringer Yenajz, drawn to Kul Tiras by the corruption of the Tidesages, has a mantle of teeth around its head that suggests the maw of C'Thun.

The most common n'raqi, faceless ones telepathically communicate with nearby creatures. Whispering into the minds of those around them, they become like gods to the weak minded and invaluable tools to those blessed with otherworldly insight. They attack both through their minds and with the strength of their two pseudopods, one of which is always much larger and more fully formed than the other.

entries.name: Naga
entries: {@i Sinister Serpentine Servants of the Old Gods}

The naga were once night elves, Highborne followers of Queen Azshara. After the War of the Ancients, Queen Azshara pledged herself and her followers to the Old God N'Zoth, who transformed them into aquatic minions. The naga vaguely resemble to their elven forms, with humanoid arms and torsos and long, snaky tails. Male naga have snakelike heads, while female naga have humanlike heads but often have four or more arms.
Myrmidons are hulking male naga who serve as front-line warriors in battles against the naga's enemies. They wield tridents with attached ropes that allow them to pull foes into melee range.
Sea witches are female naga who wield the magic of stormy seas.
Sirens are among the most powerful naga spellcasters, channeling the cold of the marine depths into mighty frost magic.

Though the Lich King couldn't infect the nerubians with his plague of undeath, he raised many dead nerubians using necromancy, turning them into crypt fiends. Crypt fiends wear the remnants of the cloth that they were mummified in and rake at their foes with their powerful claws. Crypt fiends use their webs to incapacitate their enemies, whose life force is sapped by the powerful necrotic energy in the webs' strands.

Nerubian venomancers use their lethal toxin as one of their primary weapons. Venomancers' mastery of poison extends to their webbing, which is toxic to those held within its grasp. Venomancers are quick to assault non-nerubians, driven by their rancor over their lost and scattered kingdom.

Nerubian warriors use their arachnid limbs to quickly scurry across the ground and climb onto walls and ceilings, maintaining their balance even in treacherous terrain. When attacking, they use the two arms on their humanoid torso to claw at their enemies, and these warriors often rely on their webbing to encase or restrict their foes, leaving them motionless and helpless.

The few nerubians who survived the Scourge have organized a rebellion called the Azjol-anak to retake Azjol-Nerub. Their bitterness over the loss of their kingdom has made many distrustful of anyone who isn't nerubian, and they attack whoever they come across without restraint or warning.

entries.name: Nerubians
entries: {@i Spiderlike Heirs of an Ancient Realm}

Nerubians are intelligent humanoid spiders whose once-powerful kingdom was decimated by {@book the Scourge|WoW|6|The Scourge}, leaving them either scattered across the world or turned to undead in the service of the Lich King. The nerubians evolved from the aqir, the Old Gods' insectile servitors, after the aqir's rule was overthrown by trolls. Then early nerubians founded great kingdoms: Azj-Kahet, deep within the sunken continent of Khaz Algar, and Azjol-Nerub, which extended beneath the surface of Northrend.

The nerubians of Azjol-Nerub lived in peace for thousands of years until the Lich King Ner'zhul and the Scourge conquered Northrend. The nerubians bravely resisted the Lich King's armies, resisting his plague of undeath and psychic Domination powers and holding the line against the Scourge's relentless advance, but Azjol-Nerub eventually fell to the Lich King's power. Most nerubians were either destroyed or killed and then raised into undeath, becoming crypt fiends. Those who survived remain scattered in small groups that have vowed to one day defeat the Scourge and retake their lost underground realm.
Can I just say I'm glad you survived the... oh, wait. That hasn't happened yet.

entries.name: Pit Lord
entries: {@i Hulking General of the Burning Legion}

The pit lords who fanatically serve Mannoroth the Destructor are some of the most cruel, barbarous butchers to ever roam the trackless wastes of the Great Dark Beyond. Also called annihilan, these hulking demons love only to kill and bring sorrow to living creatures. Pit lords will stop at nothing to uphold the will of the {@book Burning Legion|WoW|6|Burning Legion}.

entries.name: Prince Tortheldrin

entries: For ten thousand years I have ruled this kingdom. Is it not still glorious? Is it not still a jewel of our empire?

Prince Tortheldrin presents a genteel facade to his guests. Confident in his near invulnerability, the Highborne fears no threats and dismisses even accusations of mass murder as twaddle. He whiles away his days telling tales to his Shen'dralar sycophants but is eager for new sagas. Thus, he treats adventurers who display even a modicum of sophistication as honored guests.

When Immol'thar is slain, Tortheldrin's Demonic Invincibility trait ends, and he flies into a rage, murdering anyone in his path. When he dies, his body is reborn as a horned, winged demon. Unlike a true demon, he is permanently destroyed when killed in this form.

entries.name: Pustulant Monstrosity
entries: Pustulent monstrosities are powerful zombies found throughout Shadowfang Keep, and in particular alongside Lord Godfrey in his chamber. They are shambling hulks covered with oozing pustules filled with deadly toxin.

entries.name: Quilboar
entries: {@i Boar-Like People with Protective Spines}

Believed to be the mortal descendants of the demigod Agamaggan, a mighty boar felled during the War of the Ancients, quilboar resemble humanoid boars with a row of razor-sharp spines down their backs. They often make their homes among the large patches of thorn-covered vines on Azeroth that are believed to have been grown from Agamaggan's blood, though they have attacked nearby creatures and communities to expand their territory. Quilboar are fearless and aggressive.

The Razorfen is the mightiest quilboar tribe, and its expansion across the Barrens has driven countless smaller clans into Durotar, Mulgore, and beyond, forcing them into conflict with the Horde. The Death's Head tribe, seeking supremacy over not just the Horde but their own kin, allied with {@book the Scourge|WoW|6|The Scourge} and willingly gave themselves to undeath.

See the "{@book Furbolgs, Murlocs, and Quilboar|WoW|7|Furbolgs, Murlocs, and Quilboar}" sidebar in "{@book Murlocs|WoW|7|Murlocs}" in this chapter for suggestions on other Humanoid stat blocks to use for quilboar NPCs.
Quilboar thornweavers bear thorns they believe grew from the body of their demigod progenitor Agamaggan. Their magic uses those thorns, calling on the spirits of nature to protect their territory.

entries.name: Ragnaros
entries: {@i The Firelord, Elemental Ruler of the Firelands}

Ragnaros is the most infamous of the four great elemental lords (see {@book chapter 6|WoW|6}). Like the other elemental lords, Ragnaros warred against the Old Gods when they first came to Azeroth but eventually succumbed to their corrupting influence and became one of their mightiest servants. The titan keepers imprisoned Ragnaros on the Elemental Plane, but after millennia of rulership over his fiery prison, he was summoned back to Azeroth.

The Dark Iron dwarves accidentally called Ragnaros forth in a last-ditch effort to win a war against the other dwarven clans. Ragnaros's volcanic reemergence devastated the land for miles around and created the ashen peak of Blackrock Mountain, which now looms over Stormwind and Ironforge. The Firelord is pyroclastic devastation incarnate. He sees all mortals as insects and can't be reasoned with or bewitched. Ragnaros's worshippers include flamewakers (use the {@creature Salamander|XMM} stat block in the {@book Monster Manual|XMM}) and the Dark Iron clan.

entries.name: Ragnaros's Lair
entries: Ragnaros transforms any place he dwells into an echo of the Plane of Fire. Rock melts into pools and streams of lava, flames dance through the air, and toxic smoke bursts from vents in the ground.
The region surrounding Ragnaros's lair is scarred and scorched, creating the following effects:

items.name: Extreme Heat
items.entry: Temperatures within 1 mile of the lair are comparable to a scorching desert, subjecting creatures to {@hazard extreme heat|XDMG} (see the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG}).

items.name: Sulfurous Vapors
items.entry: Toxic gases seep up from the ground within 1 mile of the lair. A creature that finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} in that area must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw or have the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition for 1 hour.

entries: These effects are permanent scars left on the terrain by Ragnaros's presence.
Didn't we meet fighting Ragnaros's forces on Mount Hyjal? Was that the first time we met? Or will it be the last?

entries.name: Red Dragonflight
entries: {@i Noble Dragons Charged with Protecting Life}

The red dragonflight, ruled by Alexstrasza the Life-Binder, is noble and honorable. Dragons of this flight consider themselves the protectors of life. They often protect sacred areas and items, seeking to keep them from lesser beings. Their mission is to destroy existential threats to life, and they have aided in wars against the Old Gods, the {@book Burning Legion|WoW|6|Burning Legion}, the Lich King, and the black dragon aspect Deathwing—their most hated enemy.
Red dragons are likely to be allies to heroes of both the Alliance and the Horde, though some red dragons have been turned to evil by the Old Gods' corrupting whispers.

Members of the red dragonflight are considered the most noble dragons of Azeroth, sworn to protect all life. But their benevolence should never be misunderstood as weakness; they are capable of terrible destruction, outweighed only by the life-giving power that suffuses their fiery breath.

Red dragonflight drakes heal tainted lands across Azeroth. By breathing streams of blazing fire across the terrain, these drakes incinerate withered plant life and bring growth from the ashes. When need is greatest, these drakes allow mortal heroes to ride and fight on their backs.

Although red dragonflight whelps are small, their fiery breath is mighty. These creatures' sense of justice leads them to take on larger foes in the name of good. Red dragonflight whelps almost never flee from a fight, for their pride hasn't yet been tempered by the wisdom of age.

entries.name: Satyrs
entries: {@i Ancient Elves Corrupted by Fel Forces}

The first satyr was a Highborne night elf named Xavius, a servant of Sargeras during the War of the Ancients. As punishment for Xavius's failures, Sargeras destroyed the elf and remade him in a demonic form, with goatlike horns and hooves, shaggy fur, and brutal claws. Xavius's curse spread through his allies and followers, and these satyrs now live in sects with varying allegiances. They loathe their night elf kin above all else, and most of them remain devoted servants of the {@book Burning Legion|WoW|6|Burning Legion}. A few, though, have followed Xavius's example and turned to the worship of the Old Gods.

entries.name: Scarlet Champion Herod

entries: Ah, I've been waiting for a real challenge.

Herod is a charming bully who became a dazzling gladiator. The Scarlet Commander keeps him in the monastery to inspire the troops, since his tendency to cleave indiscriminately can make him a liability to his allies in combat.

entries.name: Scarlet Commander Mograine

entries: I am the son of the Ashbringer, and we are all children of the Light! It is the one true path to victory!

Renault Mograine murdered his father in cold blood on the battlefield. He was manipulated into doing so by the dreadlord Balnazzar, but that doesn't dilute his sin. Renault is haunted but zealous, and he's oblivious that his Crusade is a sham puppeted by a demon.
Shadowstalkers are satyrs who wield the subtle magic of the Void, using that power to lurk in the darkness and strike enemies from hiding.

entries.name: Shivarra
entries: {@i Towering Priest of the Burning Legion}

Devout and exceedingly charismatic, shivarra are demonic priests who shared the news of Sargeras's dread and powerful vision. They are the driving heart of the {@book Burning Crusade|WoW|6|Burning Legion}.
Bigger isn't always better, and I don't know that six arms are any better than two. Sometimes they're just nastier.

entries.name: Sneed's Shredder

entries: I made this beauty to cut down Ashenvale old growths, but there ain't no reason why she can't fell you, too!

Sneed ({@creature Goblin Boss|XMM}) was a logging engineer for the Venture Co. in Stranglethorn when {@creature Edwin VanCleef|WoW} hired him to build his Juggernaut. Sneed runs the Mast Room from his bipedal, tree-felling shredder.

entries.name: Sylvanas Windrunner
entries: {@i Vengeful Banshee}

The thirst for vengeance festers within the shadowy heart of Sylvanas Windrunner, the Banshee Queen. Her hatred is first for the {@creature Lich King Arthas|WoW|Lich King, Arthas Menethil}, who slew her and bound her soul into eternal servitude, then for {@book the Scourge|WoW|6|The Scourge} who slaughtered her people. And last, for all the living.

The Dark Lady of the Forsaken has committed terrible atrocities in the name of revenge. Her cruelty grew after the Lich King's demise, as she fell further into nihilistic despair. Hundreds of thousands of people died on her orders and were raised as her undead soldiers. Ultimately, she repented and accepted judgment for her evils and now dwells within the Shadowlands, freeing souls as eternal penance.

entries.name: Thrall
entries: {@i Liberator of the Orcs and Guardian of the Elements}

The first orc to be born on Azeroth after the Horde invaded through the Dark Portal, Thrall was an orphan of the First War and grew up in an orc internment camp. His hard life has made him stern but kind. As a leader and a shaman, he teaches his people to pursue coexistence over conflict, with both the other peoples of Azeroth and the wild elements that govern the world.

After many battles, Thrall retired to Outland to live a simple life away from war. In time, Thrall's old friends reminded him of his duty to his people, and he joined the Horde Council. He wields Dra'gora, an axe he forged in his seclusion—for even then, he knew he would one day return to defend his people.
Thrall is a great example of how you can't let other people define you.

entries.name: Twilight Lord Kelris

entries: Who dares disturb my meditation? I could all but hear the fathomless dreams of Aku'mai.

An orc shaman-turned-warlock named Kelris Doomfang found a three-headed monster in Blackfathom Deeps, Aku'mai, while fleeing justice. He became convinced it was a herald of the {@book Old Gods'|WoW|6|Old Gods} return to Azeroth and was determined to control it. Kelris gathered a sect of the Twilight's Hammer to the depths, and he supervises the monster's growth, feeding it his own subjects to satisfy its wild hunger.

Voidcallers are magic-wielding voidwalkers that appear to be draped in rotting cloth. From their shoulders hang two lanterns, which are said to bridge the realm of the living and that of the dead and sometimes attract wayward ghosts. The lanterns hang from a glowing crystalline structure that hovers over and around the voidcaller's shadowy form.
Warlocks highly prize ordinary voidwalkers as servants because of their ability to both attract and withstand enemy attacks.

entries.name: Voidwalkers
entries: {@i Creatures of Incarnate Void}
Voidwalkers are creatures of the Void, hulking figures made of pure shadow in hues of black, purple, and blue with glowing violet eyes. They are often adorned with bracers or pauldrons.
